original.target_description: Study 1, brain transplant: between-subjects judgments of identity change, moral-conscience loss versus autobiographical amnesia. Figure 1 and its caption establish this pairwise comparison; the separately printed planned contrast combines memories or desires and is not substituted for this pair.

n.sample_role: Participants in the morality and amnesia conditions; pair-specific analytic count unavailable. Printed 148 is the total across all five conditions.
n.exclusions: No exclusions or final condition counts supplied in Study 1 methods/results; no N derived from degrees of freedom.

notes: Identity independently checked: supplied canonical text presents The essential moral self, Nina Strohminger and Shaun Nichols, Cognition 131 (2014) 159–171, DOI 10.1016/j.cognition.2013.12.005, matching the neutral original reference. This is a primary research article with all 13 printed pages represented, rather than an abstract or secondary report; the cache also contains warning headers from prior text output. No PDF path supplied, so no rendering performed. Assigned fields only: n_o and es_value_o; replication, original p, and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. The explicit morality-versus-amnesia locator identifies the pairwise comparison independently of numbers or row order. Study 1 reports 148 participants across five between-subject conditions without condition-specific counts, so this recruitment/study total cannot establish the analytic N of the requested pair. Figure 1 caption bounds all pairwise comparisons except Control versus Agnosia and Apathy versus Amnesia at p < .01, including the requested pair. No pair-specific t/F statistic is printed for morality versus amnesia. Candidate evidence retained separately: planned contrast for moral deficit versus losing memories or desires, F(1,146) = 6.94, p = .009, with morality M = 4.8. The broader contrast cannot be assigned to the specific morality–amnesia pair; its p is not substituted for the pairwise bound. No effect conversion or sample-size derivation performed.
